knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux as a Double Integral Using Green's Theorem in Flux Form

question.:question/problem:
According to the flux form of Green's theorem, the flux of the vector field 
$F(x,y)=\langle 5 x^{2} + 5 y^{2},5 x^{3} + 5 y^{3}\rangle$
across the triangle $C$ with vertices $(0,0),(0,-2),$ and $(1,-1)$ can be represented as

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $C$ is traversed counterclockwise, $n$ is the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C,$ and $D$ is the region bounded by $C.$ Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/f1/f1b9472021d3973167a7601785803837627476a4e8b1460e42f87e91ecb99d7e.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=5 x^{2} + 5 y^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=5 x^{3} + 5 y^{3}.$ So,

$$
\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}=10 x,\qquad \frac{\partial Q}{\partial y}=15 y^{2} .
$$

Therefore, applying the flux form of Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\oint_C P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x &= \iint_D\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial Q}{\partial y}\right)\,\text{d}A \\ &=\iint_D\left((10 x)+(15 y^{2})\right)\,\text{d}A \\ &=\iint_D 5 \left(2 x + 3 y^{2}\right)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=5 \left(2 x + 3 y^{2}\right).$

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux as a Double Integral Using Green's Theorem in Flux Form

question.:question/problem:
Consider the rectangle $C$ with vertices $(-1,-1),(1,-1),(1,2),$ and $(-1,2),$ traversed counterclockwise. Using the flux form of Green's theorem, express the flux of the vector field
$F(x,y)=(5 x^{2} y + 30 x y)\,i+(- 5 y^{2})\,j$
through $C$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/86/861b873005c03ea6c25255f2febc975ff153d939780ec46e4f4503cbb50640dc.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=5 x^{2} y + 30 x y$ and $Q(x,y)=- 5 y^{2}.$ So,

$$
\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}=10 x y + 30 y,\qquad \frac{\partial Q}{\partial y}=- 10 y .
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\ -1\le y\le 2\} .
$$

Therefore, applying the flux form of Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\oint_C P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x &= \iint_D\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial Q}{\partial y}\right)\,\text{d}A \\ &=\iint_D\left((10 x y + 30 y)+(- 10 y)\right)\,\text{d}A \\ &=\int_{-1}^{1}\int_{-1}^{2}10 y \left(x + 2\right)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
